summary.text: Scott Houldieson is the Democratic candidate for Indiana State Senate District 1 in the November 3, 2026 general election, in which he faces Republican Trevor De Vries for a seat with no incumbent.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a 37-year member of UAW Local 551 who works at the Ford Chicago Assembly Plant.

paragraphs.text: In a Ballotpedia survey, Houldieson said he is a lifelong Lake County resident who grew up in Griffith and has lived in Highland for 25 years with his wife, Vicky; he said they have six children and thirteen grandchildren.

He said he has been a union leader and, when his union was embroiled in a corruption scandal, helped get corrupt officials expelled and led a successful effort for direct elections of its International Officers.
He also said he is a founding member of the Calumet Region chapter of Progressive Democrats of America.

Houldieson's survey responses listed priorities including lower utility rates, restored childcare vouchers, higher unemployment benefits, a living-wage minimum wage and increased public school funding.
He said he supports repealing Indiana's right-to-work law, reinstating prevailing wage legislation, and creating an infrastructure bank modeled on the Bank of North Dakota.
He listed endorsements from USW District 7, UAW Region 2B, UFCW Locals 881 and 700, Senator Bernie Sanders and the Indiana AFL-CIO.
